pr_body:
This fixes a major performance issue in the current git beta.
This PR also removes the PopoverButton component, which was easy to misuse.

Release Notes:

- Git Beta: Fix frame drops caused by opening the git panel
pr_comments: I think this may fix #25975 as well, based on the trace most of those allocations are being done by the branches popover.

issue_context.title: Git Beta: Memory leak upon pushing
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When I push a commit, regardless of repo, my zed seizes into a memory leak.

Steps to trigger the problem:
1. Create a change
2. Commit the change
3. Push the change
4. Observe memory usage spike, and frames dropping within zed.

Actual Behavior:
Memory leak. Starts to stutter. 2 different repo examples:
https://share.cleanshot.com/jRwTmDfj
https://share.cleanshot.com/wmJsX194

Expected Behavior:
Commit pushes to git.

### Zed Version and System Specs

Zed: v0.177.0 (Zed Preview) 
OS: macOS 15.2.0
Memory: 32 GiB
Architecture: aarch64

### If applicable, attach your `~/Library/Logs/Zed/Zed.log` file to this issue.

_No response_
comments: @reecepm if you're able to build Zed from source and capture a trace with the Instruments "Leaks" template when this occurs it would be invaluable! Also, is there anything noteworthy about the git remote or remotes you're using when this occurs?

> [@reecepm](https://github.com/reecepm) if you're able to build Zed from source and capture a trace with the Instruments "Leaks" template when this occurs it would be invaluable! Also, is there anything noteworthy about the git remote or remotes you're using when this occurs?

@cole-miller 

Nothing noteworthy about the git remotes - standard https remotes.

Here's a stack of running a fresh build for ~2m. Too big for here so: https://we.tl/t-ggAKWHPpbT
_If you want it uploaded/sent differently, or re-recorded in a different way lmk, it's just 2.5GB so gh isn't a fan_
@reecepm glad that fixed the leak! Re: the hang on push, how are you authenticating to the https remotes? If you're using `git-credential-manager`, this is a known issue that we're working on fixing.

Are you using Git Credential Manager for authentication, by any chance?

Ha, jynx Cole!
